content: 1. Atazanavir increases the plasma concentration and pharmacological effect of solifenacin by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Close monitoring is required. 2. Cobicistat also increases the plasma concentration and effect of solifenacin through CYP3A4 inhibition. It is recommended to avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 3. Atazanavir elevates the levels and effects of sonidegib by inhibiting CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. Avoid coadministration of sonidegib with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 4. Cobicistat increases the levels and effects of sonidegib via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 5. Atazanavir increases the plasma concentration and effect of sorafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 6. Sotarasib decreases the levels and effects of atazanavir by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, refer to the prescribing information for dosage adjustments. 7. Atazanavir increases the levels and effects of sparsentan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, interrupt sparsentan treatment. 8. Cobicistat also increases sparsentan levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, interrupt sparsentan treatment and consider dose titration when resuming therapy. 9. St. John’s Wort decreases atazanavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 10. Stiripentol, a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer, affects the metabolism of atazanavir. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Monitor coadministered CYP3A4 substrates for altered effects. 11. Cobicistat increases the levels and effects of sufentanil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is required. 12. Atazanavir also increases sufentanil levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Co-administration of sufentanil with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma concentrations, leading to prolonged or severe adverse effects, including potentially fatal respiratory depression. 14. Atazanavir increases the levels and effects of sunitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 15. Cobicistat also increases sunitinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 16. Atazanavir increases the levels of suvorexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 17. Cobicistat also increases suvorexant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 18. Atazanavir increases the levels and effects of tacrolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 19. Cobicistat also increases tacrolimus levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 20. Atazanavir increases tadalafil levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Cobicistat increases tadalafil levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Adjust tadalafil dosage for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) or erectile dysfunction (ED) as per specific recommendations. 22. Cobicistat increases talazoparib levels by inhibiting BCRP (breast cancer resistance protein). Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, monitor for adverse reactions. 23. Atazanavir increases tamoxifen levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 24. Cobicistat decreases tamoxifen effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 25. Atazanavir increases tamsulosin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 26. Cobicistat also increases tamsulosin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 27. Atazanavir increases tasimelteon levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Tazemetostat decreases atazanavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Cobicistat increases tazemetostat levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 30. Tecovirimat decreases atazanavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Tecovirimat also decreases cobicistat levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Atazanavir increases temsirolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 33. Cobicistat also increases temsirolimus levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 34. Atazanavir increases teniposide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Cobicistat increases teniposide levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 36. Tenofovir DF decreases atazanavir levels through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. 37. Tepotinib increases atazanavir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1). Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the P-gp substrate dosage as recommended. 38. Cobicistat increases terbinafine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Atazanavir also increases terbinafine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Cobicistat increases tezacaftor levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Adjust tezacaftor dosage when coadministered with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 41. Atazanavir increases theophylline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Cobicistat increases thioridazine levels through other mechanisms. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 43. Cobicistat increases tiagabine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Atazanavir also increases tiagabine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Atazanavir increases ticagrelor levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Cobicistat increases ticagrelor levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 47. Atazanavir increases timolol effects through pharmacodynamic synergy, raising the risk of hypotension, bradycardia, AV block, and prolonged PR interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Cobicistat increases timolol levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Atazanavir increases tinidazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Cobicistat also increases tinidazole levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Cobicistat increases tipranavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 52. Atazanavir and tipranavir both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Monitor closely. 53. Cobicistat increases levels of tisotumab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Atazanavir also increases tisotumab vedotin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Cobicistat increases tofacitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 56. Atazanavir also increases tofacitinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Reduce tofacitinib dosage to 5 mg daily when coadministered with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors. 57. Atazanavir increases tolterodine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 58. Cobicistat also increases tolterodine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 59. Cobicistat increases tolvaptan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 60. Atazanavir also increases tolvaptan levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. This combination is contraindicated. 61. Topiramate decreases atazanavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 62. Cobicistat increases topotecan levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1). Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 63. Atazanavir increases toremifene levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 64. Cobicistat also increases toremifene levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 65. Atazanavir increases trabectedin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 66. Cobicistat also increases trabectedin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 67. Atazanavir increases tramadol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 68. Cobicistat also increases tramadol levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely.
